svg.title: TOPAK I6 — RulesFloorBase.tla: the live definition of the rules floor, its six entries and the genesis rules that satisfy it, shared by the bootstrap modules. Definitions only: no TLC run and no proof module of its own; two theorems proved in Lean
svg.desc: The module ADR-0029 §5's bootstrap modules extend, drawn from its own text, all read at build time: the rule space, the entries, the floor, the genesis rules and their ASSUME; ADR-0026 §2's table against the module's entries; the three copies of the floor compared entry by entry; ADR-0029 §5's modules against the tree; the modules that extend this one; and the Lean re-encoding. It has no behaviour of its own: what is checked or proved of the floor is checked or proved in the modules that extend it, of their own machines. A finding is drawn as one: the module's R6 bound and genesis count predate ADR-0026 A2.

text.tspan: No TLC run of its own
Proved in Lean, of the re-encoding

svg.text: The module's header: "Shared definitions for the ADR-0029 §5 bootstrap modules: the rule space, the rules-floor entries, and the genesis rules. This is the live definition of the floor. RulesFloorNV.tla (G1) and RulesFloorNV_rev5.tla (ADR-0026 §7) each carry their own frozen copy: both are dated artifacts cited by digest in accepted records, so they are never edited. Divergence between them and this module is expected and is what the dates are for. Floor contents as ratified 2026.09.23: R1, R2, R5, R6,
R7, R9. R3 withdrawn (recusal is a mechanism constant, ADR-0024 §6) R4 withdrawn (a timeout is never a grant, ADR-0024 §2) R8 reserved, candidate (break-glass grant TTL)"

text.tspan: The definitions: the people, the acts, the rule space, the entries, the floor and the genesis rules (

svg.text: CONSTANT Active (line 17): the floor entries in force; "drop one to mutate" (its comment)
exceptions: the declared policy-floor exceptions (ADR-0013 §2), which this copy adds.

g.text: ASSUME \A e \in AllEntries : Entry(e, Genesis) (line 63): "the shape of GenesisSatisfiesFloor" (its comment;

text.tspan: 's table, every row, against the module's entries
Against the module (compared at build time)

svg.text: R1 rules.quorum = "all" (unanimity over counted grant seats)
Entry, arm R1: r.quorum.mode = "all"
Entry, arm R2: r.minGrant >= 2
struck: R3 rules.recuse = TRUE (author recusal)
Withdrawn 09.23 ⟨R1⟩. Vacuous: recusal is enforced by the ADR-0022 Vote envelope and is a mechanism constant in ADR-0024 §6, so recuse is not an issued value and this entry bounds nothing (S6-3). ID
reserved, not reused.
withdrawn, and not an entry of the module
struck: R4 Vote timeout ⇒ deny
Withdrawn 09.15. Vacuous as a rules-floor entry; moved to ADR-0024 as a mechanism constant. ID reserved, not reused.
withdrawn, and not an entry of the module
R5 No key both in the anchor key set and on the promotion roster for the same artifact
Entry, arm R5: r.grant \cap AnchorKeys = {}
R6 Bound on floor-exception count (current count: 2)
Entry, arm R6: r.exceptions <= 2
R7 No break-glass grant may authorize Issue, Vote, or promotion
ADR-0009 / ADR-0013 (discharges break-glass × issuance and break-glass × promotion)
Entry, arm R7: r.bgScope \cap AuthActs = {}
R9 rules.quorum = "all" ∨ rules.quorum ≥ 2 ⟨R1⟩

ADR-0024. Relaxing R1 alone yields a threshold *k*; without R9 that threshold may be 1, which is D-0024-2 (single signer) entering as though it were D-0024-1. R9 keeps the two degeneracies separately declared.
A conditional entry ⟨R3⟩: it binds only once R1 is relaxed, and its independence is stated relative to a floor without R1 (§7, finding 1). R8 remains reserved for the break-glass TTL candidate.
Entry, arm R9: r.quorum.mode = "all" \/ r.quorum.k >= 2

text.tspan: A finding: R6 and the genesis count predate

svg.text: ADR-0026 A2 (ratified in Batch 34): "R6 still bounds the number of floor exceptions; the count it bounds is 1, erasure."
The module: R6 is r.exceptions <= 2, and Genesis carries exceptions |-> 2, "erasure and break-glass (ADR-0013 §3)" (its comment). Its header dates its contents "as ratified 2026.09.23".
The bound still admits a count of 1; the genesis value does not match the record. The diagram's reading, for the custodian; the record is not changed by drawing it.
ADR-0026 A1: R8 would enter the table as a break-glass TTL bound. The module reserves it: "R8 reserved, candidate (break-glass grant TTL)" (its header).

text.tspan: The three copies of the floor, entry by entry (each module's

svg.text: Read from each module at build time. A row is amber where the copies differ, and plain where all three agree: R1's quorum is a string in G1's copy and tagged in the later two, R3 and R4 are withdrawn after G1, R6 is this copy's alone, and R9 is in the later two. "Divergence between them and this module is expected and is what the dates are for" (the header).

text.tspan: Against the tree at the pin (compared at build time)

g.text: Anchor.tla defines FloorPreserved (line 47); extends this module
BreakGlass.tla defines BreakGlassNeverChangesAuthority (line 52); extends this module

svg.text: The Genesis, RulesFloor and Promotion modules are not at the pin; the binding lists PromotionMeetsIssuedQuorum as owed ("the Promotion module, owed"). This module's ASSUME is "the shape of GenesisSatisfiesFloor", not that invariant. TLC checking at small constants is "recommended; it is not required" (ADR-0029 §5).
Found at build time: every module under spec/ whose EXTENDS names this one, compared with the diagram's list. RulesFloorNV.tla and RulesFloorNV_rev5.tla carry their own copies and do not extend it.

text.tspan: In Lean: the definitions re-encoded, and genesis proved to satisfy the floor
: the theorems, by induction on reachable states

svg.text: Also stated: GenesisEntries, GenesisFloor, which the results file lists and reports no axioms for.
"A theorem holds of the Lean re-encoding, not of the frozen TLA+ text" (lean/TopakSpec-results-2026.10.06b.txt)
lean/TopakSpec-results-2026.10.06b.txt are the files ADR-0053 cites. The later TopakSpec-results-2026.10.07.txt are compared, and say the same of RulesFloorBase.
GenesisEntries is the module's ASSUME, proved in Lean of the re-encoding; TLAPS has no proof module for it.
The verified object and the parameterized edge: what is proved once, and what may only subtract
The rules floor bounds every anchor issuance
From genesis to bootstrap: where the corpus stands at G12, with Batch 40
The policy floor in force, three gated stages from the genesis draft; and a fourth the reference links
Privileged paths through the floor, and the forensic floor that survives them
Break-glass is an emergency seating
Theorem to premise: what every checked or proved property rests on, and what is void at the reference
Verification map: what is checked, what is proved, what must fail, and what neither claims
How a proof is built and kept in step
Every diagram whose committed SVG names RulesFloorBase.tla, found at build time and compared with this list. Those diagrams draw the module as part of a record; this one draws the module.
